intro.author: Unknown. Jewish tradition credits Jeremiah; the writer drew on older records such as 'the book of the acts of Solomon' (11:41) and the chronicles of the kings of Israel and Judah.
intro.written: 1 and 2 Kings were originally one book, completed during the Babylonian exile (after 561 BC, see 2 Kings 25:27). Many scholars think an earlier edition existed in King Josiah's day.
intro.audience: Israelites living through or after the exile, asking how God's people lost their land, king and temple
intro.setting: The story runs from about 970 to 850 BC. It opens with David on his deathbed and Solomon's golden age, then follows the split of the nation into two kingdoms: Israel in the north and Judah in the south, with Jerusalem as Judah's capital.
intro.purpose: To show that the nation's rise and fall followed its loyalty to the LORD and his covenant, and that God kept speaking through prophets even when kings failed.
intro.bigIdea: A kingdom stands or falls on its faithfulness to God, not on its wealth, buildings or armies.
